title: The ordinary realization of the common-stage coefficient unit
statement:
theorem completedTensorOrdinaryUnit
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (X : Scheme.{u})
    (R : LocallyFiniteAdicRealization.Realization l X)
    [∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x)] :
    Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
      (ringedTensorUnitComplex.{u + 1, u, u + 1} (ProEt.topology X) (ring l X R)) ≅
      (ordinary l X R).obj (pullbackTensorCommonUnit l (PadicAlgCl l) X))

source.place: BS Lemma 6.8.2 and Remark 6.8.15; Stacks Tags 03EL, 07A4 and 0941; coefficient unit and scalar extension of the regular module.

proof.text: Choose a finite test field of characteristic different from l, by a prime larger than l. The integral regular coefficient object is constructible. Its coherent reduction and that of the reconstructed integral tensor unit are both the coherent ring unit. Fully faithful coherent reduction lifts this isomorphism to integral constructible objects.

The regular coefficient sheaf in degree zero is K-flat: tensoring with it is the right unitor, so it preserves acyclicity. Thus the prescribed derived scalar-extension counit is invertible on this complex. The single-complex comparison and sheafified scalar multiplication identify its extension with the target regular coefficient sheaf in degree zero.

At the least finite coefficient field, compose the inverse derived regular-module comparison, the integral tensor-unit comparison, and the inverse specified integral realization isomorphism. The definition of the common-stage coefficient unit identifies the final object.

proof_origin.place: Explicit finite normalized scalar comparisons and the coefficient unit, split from new-sf-adic-completed-tensor-common-lift-tensor-unit.
